content.text:
I built `/work/spec.vl.json` and it renders with no errors or warnings. The answer to the question is no: the peak timing has changed since 2020.

- **Before 2020:** every season peaked in ISO weeks 5–12 (February–March).
- **Since 2020:**
  - 2020/21 had no winter peak; its highest week was week 39.
  - 2021/22 peaked in March 2022 (week 11).
  - 2022/23 and 2023/24 peaked in December (week 50).
  - 2024/25 and 2025/26 were back in February (weeks 7 and 6).

**Not tested:** dragging on the linear view. The render only produces a still image, so I couldn't confirm that the circle highlights the selected weeks.

The figure has a cyclic view on the left (one line per ISO year, week 1 at the top, clockwise) and the full 2012–2026 series on the right. Season peaks are marked in both views.

```
REPORT
deliverable: spec.vl.json
requirements:
  R1: done - angle = 2π(week−1)/weeks-in-ISO-year, W1 at 12 o'clock, clockwise; radius = incidence (x/y computed with sin/cos)
  R2: done - one line per ISO year, viridis colour with "ISO year" legend
  R3: done - highest week per Saison marked with black-outlined point and season label (circle and linear view)
  R4: done - linear line chart on a temporal axis, 2012-W40 to 2026-W43, date = Monday of ISO week
  R5: done - x-interval brush in linear view filters coloured circle lines/peaks; unselected weeks remain as faint grey (drag not tested in a live browser)
  R6: done - W1…W49 labels around circle, grey rings labelled 1,000–4,000 with radius unit note; year axis; y title with unit
  R7: done - title plus caption sentence (subtitle) on peak timing
assumptions:
  - ISO week date computed as Monday of the week (from Jan 4 rule) within the spec
  - Years with 53 ISO weeks use 53 angular steps; week labels drawn on a 52-week grid
  - Peak ties resolved by the earliest week; 2026/27 (only 4 weeks so far) still marked, but as a diamond labelled "season in progress"
  - Ring spacing (1,000) is a design choice; the outer ring is the data max rounded up to the next 1,000
limitations:
  - Each year's line ends at week 52/53 and is not connected to week 1 of the next year (small gap at the top)
  - The caption text is written by hand from the data; everything plotted is computed in the spec
  - The circle is visually dense; the brush is the main way to isolate individual years
  - Light yellow (most recent years) has lower contrast on white
```
